item.title: Russia releases imprisoned U.S. citizen Stephen Hubbard following Trump's request
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin says he has freed an American, Stephen Hubbard, from a Russian prison following a request from President Trump.

item.title: France announces nightly curfews 'for as long as necessary' in Paris and other cities
item.description: Fresh curfews were being imposed across the city centers of Paris and Lyon on Tuesday after the first quiet night since France's most destructive rioting in years.

item.title: Current U.S. support for Ukraine looks very different than it did
item.description: NPR's Scott Detrow talks with William Taylor, former U.S. Ambassador to Ukraine, about President Trump's recent moves to support Russia and how that compares to past administrations.

item.title: Nigeria confirms an Ebola case in Abuja as a woman arriving from Uganda tests positive
item.description: Nigeria is the latest country to report an Ebola case as the outbreak spreads across the region. Kenya confirmed its first case earlier this month and has since recorded nine infections.

item.title: DOJ charges 28 with voting crimes. And, TikTok ignored staff's child safety concerns
item.description: The Justice Department has charged 28 people in California with voting crimes as Election Day nears. And, TikTok staff raised child safety concerns with executives, who failed to act, court records show.

item.title: Trump makes Russia-friendly moves as he looks for a way to end the war with Ukraine
item.description: President Trump's up and down relationship with Russia is back on as he presses to find an end to the war in Ukraine amid high energy costs ahead of the U.S. midterms.

item.title: Former U.S. ambassador on Trump's recent moves to embrace Russia
item.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with former U.S. Ambassador to Russia Michael McFaul about President Trump's latest embrace of Russia and what it means for Ukraine and any hopes of peace.

item.title: Alberta voters reject a move toward independence in referendum backing Canadian unity
item.description: Voters in Canada's oil-rich Alberta province overwhelmingly backed remaining in Canada, with early referendum results Tuesday delivering a boost to Prime Minister Carney's push for national unity.
item.content:encoded:
Voters in Canada's oil-rich Alberta province overwhelmingly backed remaining in Canada, with early referendum results Tuesday delivering a boost to Prime Minister Carney's push for national unity.

(Image credit: James Maclennan)

item.title: Alberta voters decide whether to take a step toward separating from Canada
item.description: In Canada, the oil-rich province of Alberta votes in a referendum that could set it on a path toward separation, as Prime Minister Mark Carney warns of threats to Canadian unity.
